messages.subject: predict.oSCR
parts:
Dear all,

According to my knowledge, the function "predict.oSCR" still does not work with sex covariants. ("We added some basic prediction capacity (see ?predict.oSCR for some terse information abut this).   Does not yet work for models with "sex" as a covariate")

So how one can compute the density in a Raster  by sex type?

Are some news about this interesting subtopic.

Best wishes!

Victor

messages.subject: RE: [oscr] predict.oSCR
parts:
Clayton is right here (although I believe he should be finishing his thesis right now J, hope all is going well man!).

 

I can’t remember why predict.oSCR() doesn’t/wouldn’t work for sex structured models? Have you tested it to see if you get an error?

 

How to proceed here depends on a couple of things.

 

1.       Are you interested in making maps of expected or realized density

2.       Do you have spatial (density) covariates

 

If you answered realized for (1) then predict.oSCR() is what you need. Let me know what happens when you try it.

 

If you answered expected for (1) then get.real() is your friend. If you just do get.real(model, type= “dens”), i.e., don’t provide a newdata object, the function will return predictions for exactly the state space used to fit the model. Then you could do something like:

 

#untested

preds <- get.real(model, type= “dens”)

rast.preds <- raster::rasterFromXYZ(cbind(model$ssDF[[1]]$X, model$ssDF[[1]]$Y,preds$estimate))

 

Note that the preds object will be 2x the number of pixels because there will be a male and a female prediction, so you will need to subset the preds object.

 

Hope this helps, but if not, I can have another crack at the troubleshooting later when I have a bit more time.

 

Chris
